title: When the Wreck Breaks
premise: Orsen Ravensworth has spent eleven years piloting the riverboat Vesper's Wake up and down the Kestrel River, outrunning debts, memories, and anyone foolish enough to call her family. When a spring flood coughs up a sealed chest stamped with the crest of Vhalen—a nation drowned under treaty and rumor a generation ago—every faction on the river wants it: the harbor syndicate, a disgraced imperial surveyor, and a girl named Tamsin who claims the seal is her birthright. Orsen agrees to haul them north only as far as the mountain port, but the chest's contents force her to choose between the anonymity she's bought with distance and the belonging she's been fleeing. The journey becomes a race across the Corvane Range ahead of the snows, through the glacier pass that opens for mere weeks during calving season. In the end, Orsen loses the boat that defined her but gains a crew worth calling home—and learns that survival bought alone is just a slower way of drowning.
about_author: Marguerite Nakamura grew up in a family of tugboat pilots on the Pacific coast and spent a decade working seasonal river freight before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for their weather-wise prose and crews of misfits who argue their way into becoming families.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A routine run down the Kestrel establishes her world: the boat, her taciturn deckhand Pell, and the sandbars she reads like faces. She refuses a passenger at dock—refusal is habit. Emotional beat: competence as armor; we see how carefully she avoids attachment.

chapters.title: What the Flood Gave Back
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. After a night storm, the river deposits a waterlogged chest against the Vesper's hull. Inside: documents bearing the drowned seal of Vhalen. Pell urges throwing it back; Orsen hesitates too long. Beat: curiosity cracking the shell of self-preservation.

chapters.title: A Girl With a Dead Country's Eyes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The girl tracks Orsen to a riverside tavern and claims the chest—and the name inside it—as hers. She's fierce, half-starved, and lying about something. Beat: Orsen recognizes a survivor's hunger because she wears one herself.

chapters.title: Buyers at the Dock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Harbor syndicate men make an offer for the chest, then a threat. Orsen realizes keeping it has painted a target on her boat. She agrees to carry Tamsin north to the mountain port—for a price. Beat: greed dressed as pragmatism.

chapters.title: The Surveyor Who Fell
chapters.summary: Davor Hale's POV. Introduce the disgraced imperial surveyor who once mapped the Corvane passes before his maps were used to betray Vhalen. He begs passage, offering knowledge of the glacier route. Beat: guilt seeking redemption through usefulness.

chapters.title: Crew of Convenience
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Upstream through narrowing gorges; friction among passengers. Tamsin and Hale spar over Vhalen's history while Pell quietly teaches Tamsin rope work. Beat: the accidental shape of a crew forming despite Orsen's resistance.

chapters.title: Syndicate Smoke
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. A syndicate gunboat shadows them; a nighttime chase through fog banks. Orsen threads shallows no charted pilot would dare. Beat: fear bonding the group; Pell sees Orsen almost smile and worries what that costs her.

chapters.title: The Chest Speaks
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin finally reveals the truth: the chest holds proof of who sold Vhalen to its conquerors—including a signature connected to Hale's old expedition. Beat: betrayal detonates trust; the crew fractures mid-river.

chapters.title: Marooned at Gray Landing
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Stranded by low water and mutual suspicion, Hale confesses his role—not as traitor, but as the man whose honest maps were weaponized. Orsen must decide whether truth or utility matters more. Beat: the price of survival measured in trust.

chapters.title: Last Port Before the Range
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The mountain port of Coldharbour: mule trains, calving-season rumors, and syndicate agents everywhere. Orsen plans to hand off the chest and be done—but finds she can't make herself do it. Beat: the first involuntary act of loyalty.

chapters.title: Snowline Bargains
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. To cross legally they need permits; to get permits they need leverage. Tamsin trades a piece of the chest's contents to a Coldharbour archivist, secretly keeping the crucial page. Beat: Tamsin becoming a strategist; secrets multiplying.

chapters.title: The Pass Opens Early
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Word comes: the glacier route will open days early—and close early too, squeezed by an approaching storm system. They must leave tomorrow or winter in Coldharbour with the syndicate. Beat: the clock starts; commitment becomes irreversible.

chapters.title: Switchbacks and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. First days on the trail. Orsen, a river creature, is clumsy on ice; Tamsin, mountain-born, quietly steadies her. Role reversal deepens their bond. Beat: vulnerability exchanged like currency.

chapters.title: The Frozen Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned tollhouse, they find evidence the syndicate sent riders ahead. Pell proposes turning back; Orsen, for the first time, chooses forward. Beat: Pell's quiet heartbreak—he knows where this road ends for her.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Serac Field
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Syndicate riders attack among the ice towers. Hale takes a wound shielding Tamsin; they drive the attackers off only when a serac collapses, killing two pursuers. Beat: violence strips away pretense; the crew is now complicit in each other's survival.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Burying the dead, Tamsin confronts what reclaiming Vhalen would actually require—and whether she wants a country or a family. She burns the page she kept secret. Beat: the theme made explicit; choosing people over legacy.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The glacier begins to calve early, the pass groaning shut behind them. A crevasse field must be crossed in a shrinking window of stable cold. Beat: nature as indifferent antagonist; awe and terror braided together.

chapters.title: Rope and Ruin
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Pell falls into a crevasse; the rescue nearly kills them all. Orsen realizes the boat—the last piece of her old life—is already gone, scuttled at Coldharbour by syndicate agents. There is nothing left to return to. Beat: rock bottom; grief as clearing.

chapters.title: The Summit Window
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Final ascent through the closing storm window, carrying wounded Hale, following Tamsin's mountain instincts and Orsen's weather-reading fused into one skill. Beat: the found family functioning as a single organism.

chapters.title: Descent Into Vhalen's Valley
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They descend into the hidden valley where Vhalen's survivors endured in exile. Tamsin is offered a place as heir—with strings that would cost her the crew. Beat: belonging offered on terms; the final test.

chapters.title: The Seal Broken Open
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax. Syndicate agents arrive via the southern pass, demanding the chest. In the confrontation, the valley elders read the documents aloud: the truth of Vhalen's fall, Hale vindicated, the syndicate exposed. Orsen stands, publicly, as Tamsin's chosen kin. Beat: every debt called in at once; courage as declaration.

chapters.title: A Boat Worth Building
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Resolution. Spring: the valley funds a new vessel, and Orsen, Hale, Pell, and Tamsin lay her keel together—the Vesper's Wake reborn. Orsen stops moving, not because stopping is safe, but because she finally has somewhere worth being still. Beat: arrival; the price of survival paid, and worth it.
